paragraphs: Rava. Rav Adda son of Rava; Rav Huna son of Rava; Rav Haviva bar Rava—needs examination; Rav Hanan, Rav's pupil, son of Rava; Rav Yosef bar Rava; Rav Menashya bar Rava; Mar Keshisha bar Rava; Rav Mesharshiya bar Rava; Rav Nahman bar Rava; Rav Sama bar Rava; Rav Anan bar Rava; Rabbah bar Rava. [Glosses: Rava and Rabbah. (1) Sukkah 53a [folio notation malformed in the source]: Abaye was walking before Rava; it should read Rabbah. (2) Eruvin 49b: ‘Rabbah said that R' Hama bar Gurya said.’ Nowhere in the entire Talmud do we find Rabbah speaking in his name. Perhaps it should read Ravin bar Rav Huna, whom we do find speaking in his name: רב״ה is an abbreviation for Ravin bar Huna. Not corrected [ל״ת, provisionally “not corrected”, here and below]. (3) Bava Batra 174a: Mar bar Amemar told Rav Ashi, ‘Thus my father said’; so too in Rif. In Asheri, ‘Rava said’ is a scribal error. (4) Bava Kamma 97, end of a: Rava spoke to Rav Yehudah. Perhaps it should read Rabbah, since Rava was born the day Rav Yehudah died; not corrected. (5) Yoma 50a: Ravin bar Rav Adda told Rava, ‘Your pupil’—‘your pupils say’ is the required reading, as in the new Shas—‘Rav Amram said.’ In Zevahim 93b, ‘he said to Rav, your pupil said,’ should read ‘to Rava’; not corrected. In Mo'ed Katan 24a, ‘your pupil Rav Amram said’ should read ‘your pupils say that Rav Amram said’; not corrected. (6) Ketubbot 111a: Rava said to Rav Ashi. This is a scribal error, for Rav Ashi was born on the day Rava died. Ein Yaakov has ‘Ravina to Rav Ashi.’ (7) Avodah Zarah 27b: Rava said that R' Yohanan said. Perhaps it should read Rabbah; not corrected. (8) Nedarim 59a: Rav Hisda told Rava, ‘Who listens to you and to your teacher R' Yohanan?’ Yet Rava was not R' Yohanan's pupil. Perhaps it should read ‘Rabbah,’ as is also evident in Shevuot 10b. In the new Shas the margin prints ‘another version: Rava.’ (9) Bava Kamma 97a: Rav Yosef bar Hama, etc.; ‘Rabbah his son said to him’ should read Rava. (10) In Tosafot, Hullin 133a: ‘Rava told his attendant’—we read Rava, for Rabbah was a priest, as found in Ad Kammah, where Rabbah nullified; we also say Abaye and Rava came from Eli's house. This is how it should read; there is a scribal error in Tosafot, not corrected. (11) Shabbat 142a: R' Hiyya bar Ashi said that Rava said; it should read Rav. (12) Shabbat 129a: Rav in Rav Yehudah's name should read Rava, as in Tosafot, since Yoma 79a has Rava in Rav Yehudah's name. (13) Sotah 44a: ‘You may even say R' Yosi the Galilean, according to Rabbah, for Rabbah said’ is a scribal error and should read ‘according to Rava,’ as in Kiddushin 78a, where Rava said this and disagrees with Abaye. (14) Pesahim 117b: Rava bar Natan, father of Rav Huna bar Natan—perhaps ‘brother’ should be read; the new Shas has Rav Natan, father of Rav Huna bar Natan. (15) Shabbat 112b: Rava bar Zimuna. It seems to me it should read R' Abba bar Zimuna; not corrected. (16) Temurah 21a: Rava bar Rav Azza should read Aha bar Azza, since immediately there it has Rav Aha bar Rav Azza; not corrected. (17) Sanhedrin 98b: Rava said, ‘Let him come, but may I not see him.’ It should read Rabbah, as in the new Shas in the name of ב״ש [work abbreviation unresolved]. Immediately afterward, ‘Abaye asked Rava, “Why did you say, May I not see him?”’ should read Rabbah; not corrected. (18) Shevuot 31a; Shabbat 10a, 66b, 89, end of a, 104b, 121b; Berakhot 45a: Rava bar Rav Huna should read Rabbah bar Rav Huna; not corrected. (19) Menahot 39a: Rabbah sat and said in Shmuel's name, in the new Shas. (20) Menahot 15b: Rava Zuti should read Rabbah; the new Shas has R' Abba. (21) Pesahim 110a: Rava bar Levai should read Rabbah; not corrected. (22) Shabbat 148a; Eruvin 14, end of b, 38, end of b, 68, beginning of a; Beitzah 30a; Menahot 14b; Keritot 18b: Rava bar Hanan; in many places Rabbah. Not corrected. (23) Eruvin 45: Rabbah bar Rav Hana should read Hanan. (24) Menahot 40a: Rava bar Hana should read Rabbah bar Hanan; not corrected. (25) Bava Metzia 108a: Rabbah bar Rav Nahman; Menahot 41a, Shabbat 119a, Yevamot 25a: Rava bar Rav Nahman. Which is correct needs examination; not corrected. (26) Gittin 32a: Rabbah bar Aivu; Ketubbot 23a: bar Avin. Not corrected. (27) Nazir 38, end of b: Ravina of Parzaki should read Rava. (28) Yevamot 59b: Rava of Parkin should read ‘of Parzaki’; not corrected. (29) Shabbat 120b, 156a; Menahot 87a; Sotah 35, end of b; Zevahim 38b: Rava bar Sheila, as in many places, whereas many places have Rabbah bar Sheila. Which is right needs examination; not corrected. (30) Yoma 39, beginning of b: Rabbah bar bar Sheila—one ‘bar’ is a scribal error; not corrected. (31) Shabbat 7a should read: Rabbah bar Sheila said, ‘When Rav Dimi came’; not corrected. (32) Shabbat 95a; Sukkah 32a; Zevahim 81b: Rava Tosfa'ah should read Rabbah; not corrected. (33) Bava Batra 93, end of b: Rabbah bar Hiyya Ketosfa'ah in Rabbah's name. But Asheri, Rif, and Jerusalem Talmud, Kilayim, beginning of chapter 2, have ‘in Rav's name.’ (34) Sukkah 3a: Rabbah bar Adda; most places have Rava. Not corrected. (35) Pesahim 13a: Rabbi bar Rav Adda should read Rava or Ravin; so too in the new Shas. (36) Zevahim 95b: Rabbah bar Ahilei; immediately there, Ahilai. Not corrected. (37) Shabbat 136a: son of R' Idi bar Avin should read Rava son of ר״א ב״א [provisionally R' Idi bar Avin from the preceding full form], as in Asheri and Yuhasin. (38) Pesahim 36a: Rava bar Yirmeyah should read Rabbah, as in the new Shas; Berakhot 43a has Rava. Not corrected. (39) Zevahim 90b; Horayot 13a; Sanhedrin 100a; Yevamot 62b; Eruvin 86, beginning of a: Rava bar Mari; many places have Rabbah. Not corrected. (40) Eruvin 40a: Rava bar Tahlifa should read Rabbah; not corrected. (41) Sanhedrin 74, end of a, 98b: Rava bar Rav Yitzhak; there, 99b: Rabbah bar Rav Yitzhak; Sotah 46b: Rava bar R' Yitzhak. This needs examination; not corrected. (42) Sukkah 29, beginning of a: Rabbah bar Hama should read Rami ב״ת [patronymic abbreviation unresolved]; not corrected. (43) Nedarim 77, end of a: Rav attended to Rabbah in the small room of Rav's academy. This needs examination, for Rabbah did not see Rav; not corrected in the new Shas. Yuhasin has ‘Rav attended to Rav Hananel’; see Seder Tannaim Ve-Amoraim, under Rav Ika bar Avin. (44) Zevahim 45, beginning of a: Rava objected, ‘A halakhah for the messianic age?’ Tosafot, Yoma 13, write that Rav Yosef raised this objection. (45) Sukkah 32, beginning of b: Rabbah bar Mari in Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai's name should read ‘bar Maryon, of Rabban Yohanan ben Zakkai's household,’ as in Eruvin 19a; see Rashi there. Not corrected. (46) Shevuot 17, end of b: ‘Rabbah examined it’ should read Rava; not corrected.]
